items.title: No Matter Who You Are: Addressivity and Sycophancy in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Sycophancy, where an LLM becomes overly agreeable, deferential, or flattering toward the user, has been identified as a major failure mode. While post-training has been implicated as a cause, how it internally gives rise to sycophantic behavior remains insufficiently understood. Post-training transforms the model's output from text completion into utterances directed toward an addressee, thereby giving the output \textit{addressivity}. We hypothesize that the accompanying pressure to follow the addressee's instructions and align with their preferences links this addressivity to sycophancy. To test this, we use Sparse Autoencoders to extract addressivity directions from pre-trained and post-trained models and examine their relationship with sycophancy. Steering models with addressivity directions can amplify or suppress sycophancy, and this effect is observed only in post-trained models. Furthermore, comparing the internal mechanisms of both model types confirms that the association between addressivity and sycophancy is strengthened through post-training. Finally, through a controlled post-training experiment, we find that models are sycophantic not toward a specific addressee but toward any recognized addressee, suggesting that the presence of an addressee, rather than the addressee's identity, is what elicits sycophancy.

items.title: Novel Mobile Digital Assistive Technologies in Australia
items.abstract: Abstract For the health sector, novel applications involving automated decision-making (ADM) and artificial intelligence (AI) are seen as a way to fill critical gaps in health systems and improve patient care and outcomes. For patients, carers, and health consumers more broadly, these innovations may be viewed as a way to improve their agency and understanding of their bodies and health states. Yet, many of the devices and software remain speculative or in limited pilot testing. In this chapter, we discuss findings from a project that sought to identify the socio-technical imaginaries of ADM and AI in health in Australia, comparing “actually existing ADM” with proposed imaginaries of the futures of ADM. We mapped how emerging health technologies are discussed in industry reports and websites. Our findings reveal that these complex assemblages of people, objects, data, spaces, systems, promises, expectations, and proximities generate a number of ethical issues and power dynamics.

items.title: O serviço de referência na era da inteligência artificial: desafios, mediação da informação e novas competências bibliotecárias
items.abstract: This article aimed to analyze the changes in reference services resulting from the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and generative AI, identifying ethical, conceptual, and operational challenges, as well as the new skills and educational guidelines required for information professionals. It used a qualitative, exploratory, and descriptive bibliographic and documentary research method, based on contemporary literature on Information Science, information mediation, and emerging technologies in education. It highlights that automation and conversational assistants (like chatbots and recommendation systems) streamline operational processes and speed up access and personalization of searches; however, human mediation remains essential to ensure information literacy, critical evaluation of sources, accuracy in data retrieval, and mitigation of algorithmic hallucinations. It can be concluded that artificial intelligence doesn’t replace the librarian, but rather reshapes their role for strategic tasks, ethical oversight, and digital curation, showing that the future of reference services lies in the convergence of technological efficiency and humanized mediation.

items.title: Occupational Health and Safety of Nigerian Air Force Personnel, Infantry Soldiers and Mechanized Armoured Tank Crews: Evidence from Nigeria, Europe and the United States of America
items.abstract: Military occupational health and safety (OHS) is inseparable from operational readiness, personnel welfare and the long-term sustainability of armed forces. Nigerian Air Force personnel, infantry soldiers and mechanized armoured-vehicle crews encounter overlapping but occupationally distinctive hazards: aircraft noise and vibration, jet-fuel and exhaust exposure, fatigue and high-consequence decision-making in aviation; combat trauma, heavy load carriage, heat strain, sleep disruption and musculoskeletal injury among infantry; and whole-body vibration, acoustic trauma, restricted egress, heat, fumes and communication difficulties among armoured crews. This article examines these risks in Nigeria while drawing comparisons with research and prevention approaches from Europe, North America and other military settings. It adopts a structured narrative literature review methodology, synthesising peer-reviewed research, systematic reviews, occupational health guidance, and relevant Nigerian studies published mainly between 2023 and 2026, alongside foundational work where recent evidence is limited. Recent reviews show that military and law-enforcement populations experience a broad spectrum of adverse outcomes, including mental ill-health, hearing loss, musculoskeletal disorders, heat illness, sleep problems and burnout. Nigerian evidence identifies psychological distress among deployed soldiers and air-force personnel, while international studies provide more detailed evidence on load carriage, jet-fuel exposure, fatigue, noise and vibration. The article argues that Nigeria requires a role-specific, prevention-led military OHS system supported by exposure monitoring, confidential health surveillance, fatigue-risk management, equipment maintenance, heat controls, hearing conservation, post-deployment support and a stronger local research programme. Because available Nigerian studies are often cross-sectional or facility-specific, international findings should inform, not substitute for local exposure measurement and longitudinal research.

items.title: Occupational Health Hazards and Socio-Economic Realities of Tribal Women: A Clinical Review
items.abstract: This study evaluates the intersection of socio-economic vulnerabilities and occupational health hazards among tribal women in India. Drawing exclusively upon secondary data, government reports and academic literature, the paper highlights that an overwhelming majority of tribal women are concentrated in primary sectors-predominantly agriculture, minor forest produce collection and unorganized manual labor. Despite serving as the backbone of the tribal agrarian and forest-based economy, they face severe structural disadvantages, including deep-seated illiteracy, acute poverty, geographic isolation and an absence of ergonomically sound tools. Consequently, they experience disproportionate rates of musculoskeletal disorders, chronic fatigue, dermatological infections, vector-borne diseases and respiratory complications. The findings indicate that poor socio-economic status directly exacerbates occupational vulnerability, compounded by an acute lack of institutional healthcare infrastructure in remote tribal habitations.

items.title: OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH IN INDIA: A NEED FOR A PREVENTIVE AND ACCOUNTABLE WORKPLACE CULTURE
items.abstract: Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) has become an increasingly important concern in India as industrialisation, urbanisation, technological development, and the expansion of employment continue to reshape the world of work. Workplace safety is no longer limited to preventing machinery-related accidents or physical injuries. Workers may face chemical exposure, biological risks, unsafe equipment, poor ergonomics, occupational diseases, excessive working hours, workplace violence, stress, and other psychosocial risks. These concerns exist across sectors, including construction, manufacturing, mining, chemical industries, agriculture, informal employment, and healthcare. India has developed a substantial legal framework for protecting workers, culminating in the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, which came into force on November 21, 2025. However, the existence of legislation alone cannot guarantee safe working conditions. The continuing occurrence of workplace accidents, under-reporting of occupational diseases, inadequate safety infrastructure, and institutional failures demonstrate the need for stronger implementation and accountability. Recent attention to workplace safety following the R.G. Kar Medical College incident has further shown that occupational safety also includes dignity, security, gender-sensitive protection, and psychological well-being. The central concern, therefore, should be to move from a culture that reacts to accidents towards one that identifies and prevents risks before workers are harmed. Keywords: Occupational Safety and Health; Occupational Hazards; Workplace Safety; Occupational Diseases; Worker Protection.

items.title: OCTA Working Paper: Operationa Continuity and Turnaround Architecture, Theoretical Foundations, Quantitative Model, and Multi-Domain Validation Framework
items.abstract: This working paper sets out the theoretical foundations of the Operational Continuity and Turnaround Architecture (OCTA), a domain-free quantitative model for predicting, detecting and arresting operational collapse in complex sociotechnical systems. The two core constructs are the Dependency Cascade Index (DCI), which measures the ratio of active dependencies to remaining recovery capacity in real time, and the intervention window W(t), which measures the time remaining before DCI crosses the irreversible collapse threshold. Together these constructs enable early detection of cascade propagation and provide a formal basis for turnaround intervention before collapse becomes irreversible. The model is validated primarily in civil aviation, using GNSS interference and ADS-B signal degradation as observable proxies for DCI dynamics. Domain-independence of the W(t) mechanism is demonstrated across banking and financial systems, automotive supply chains, nuclear energy, maritime operations, power grid infrastructure and healthcare systems. This working paper is part of a PhD research programme at Cranfield University. The commercial implementation of OCTA is developed through the TYRAXE technology stack (AIX, LINK, FLOW). Patent pending.

items.title: On Data Scaling in Tabular ML: More Data, Better Generalization?
items.abstract: Recent work in tabular machine learning has emphasized the importance of diverse and realistic evaluation settings. The niche of large-scale (1M+) data, however, remains under-explored. To study training-data scaling, we assemble eight real-world tabular datasets with up to around ten million training examples, retaining the natural distribution shifts of the tasks and using random-split evaluation as a control. We find that GBDTs and MLP-based models show broadly similar scaling trends, with gains from both additional training data and algorithmic improvements. Tabular foundation models show more varied scaling behavior, with recent versions benefiting more consistently from larger contexts even under distribution shift. However, scaling training data under distribution shift introduces new challenges: in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance mostly improve together at smaller scales but can diverge at larger scales. We examine this through MLP capacity sweeps and comparisons of the validation distributions used for tuning and early stopping in MLPs and GBDTs. We also compare common practices of using validation data, contrasting its use for model selection in MLP pipelines with using it for in-context fitting in tabular foundation model pipelines. Under stronger shifts, MLPs selected using validation representative of the evaluation conditions generally maintain or improve performance as training data grows. In contrast, including such examples in context improves foundation-model performance, but does not prevent deterioration with increasing training size in our experiments.

items.title: On the LLM Verification for Argument Graph Generation
items.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems can formalize natural-language argumentation end-to-end, turning plain text into structured graphs by classifying components, connecting them with relations, and enriching the resulting graphs into formal models. Quality assurance for those graphs is almost always another LLMs: a reviewer, judge, or critic agent. On the other side, in adjacent neuro-symbolic fields, such generated output is often verified symbolically by external checks and solvers. In this work, we argue that in argument graph verification, the allocation should be similar, and based on what each instrument can guarantee. We propose layered verification: starting from deterministic checks, moving to solver-based and LLM reviews, and utilizing debate only under uncertainty, leaving human judgment for what no other instrument can decide. We ground our principle with a study on human-annotated graphs with injected structural defects. An LLM reviewer detects them at near-ceiling recall, including cycles in the support relation, but it objects to almost one in a ten correct graphs, even though it should not, happens to be inconsistent in verdict on identical inputs and is significantly slower than the equivalent exact check. It shows that while LLM reviewer does not lack the ability to detect structural defects, it is worth having a deterministic verification gates.

items.abstract: ORBITAL ARCHAEOLOGY: THE AI EARTH MAPPER TV Series Format Bible & Pitch Deck LOGLINE: Over 90% of human history remains buried beneath dense canopy, desert sands, and coastline sediments. By fusing multispectral satellite imaging, predictive AI algorithms, and precision drone LiDAR, an elite investigative team reveals lost cities and forgotten empires in real time — straight from orbit to the ground. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: Traditional archaeology is slow, costly, and bound by bureaucratic restrictions. "Orbital Archaeology: The AI Earth Mapper" revolutionizes the genre by taking exploration into the 21st century. Rather than digging blindly, the series utilizes satellite multispectral signatures (infrared, thermal, and moisture retention analysis) processed by custom Artificial Intelligence. items.title: Overuse and False Restraint in Large Language Model Recommendations for Choosing Wisely Scenarios
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Choosing Wisely initiative made recommendations where screening, testing, or treatment may be overused, with caveats around appropriate use. Clinicians are increasingly using large language models (LLMs). OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether commercial LLMs appropriately call for restraint or action from scenarios based on Choosing Wisely recommendations. DESIGN: Benchmark evaluation. Fifteen Choosing Wisely recommendations were used to develop 225 scenarios (per recommendation, 10 in which restraint was appropriate and 5 in which action was appropriate). Six commercial LLMs (3 runs each) generated 4050 responses to the 225 scenarios, using a prompt from the clinician perspective. SETTING: Production application programming interfaces of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google from February to March 2026. PARTICIPANTS: No human participants were involved. MEASUREMENTS: Co-primary outcomes were the overuse rate (endorsing action when restraint was appropriate) and the false restraint rate (withholding an appropriate action). RESULTS: The rate of LLM-recommended overuse was 5.4% (95% CI, 0.6% to 12.2%); LLMs did not recommend overuse in 8 of 15 recommendations. Two recommendations accounted for most LLM-recommended overuse: thyroid ultrasound for an incidental subcentimeter nodule (overuse recommended in 42.8% of LLM responses) and routine electrocardiography in low-risk adults (overuse recommended in 28.3% of LLM responses). The LLMs recommended overuse in 0.6% to 3.3% of responses for the remaining 5 recommendations. False restraint was rare (0.6% [CI, 0.1% to 1.2%]), was absent for 11 of 15 recommendations, and was highest for prostate-specific antigen screening (3.3%). LIMITATIONS: Single prompts without follow-up; a benchmark rather than real-world use; responses classified by LLM judge with physician adjudication. Findings may not extend to consumer-facing use. CONCLUSION: The LLMs rarely withheld recommendations for treatment when it was appropriate. Overuse was concentrated in 2 recommendations. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: None.

items.title: Palliative Care in Surgery: Updated Research Priorities from the Surgical Palliative Care Research Expert Consensus Conference
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Surgical palliative care (SPC) research has advanced since the 2017 research agenda, but persistent gaps in patient selection, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement limit implementation across evolving surgical care settings. STUDY DESIGN: In November 2025, a national consensus conference convened 28 SPC experts and researchers. Through iterative discussion and consensus-building during the meeting and subsequent months, participants updated research priorities across the surgical continuum and health system context. Full methodology and participant attributes were described in Supplemental Materials https://links.lww.com/JACS/A821. RESULTS: The updated agenda identified 11 research gaps across 3 priority areas: patient selection; interventions, care processes, and competencies; and outcome measurement. Priorities were mapped at 2 levels: surgical episodes, encompassing patient-, family-, and provider-level factors, and health systems, encompassing organizational and structural factors affecting SPC delivery. The agenda prioritizes identifying which patients benefit from SPC and when; broadening SPC beyond traditional populations; defining primary SPC competencies and the role of specialty consultation; improving communication of surgical intent, trade-offs, and preference-sensitive decisions; integrating and sustaining SPC across heterogeneous systems and care transitions; transforming clinical cultures; and developing patient-centered, context-specific surgical and systems-level outcomes. Emerging electronic health record, natural language processing, and large language model approaches may support scalable patient identification, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement, while requiring attention to bias and task-dependent performance. CONCLUSIONS: SPC research should move beyond narrow proof-of-concept settings toward pragmatic, scalable approaches that define who should receive SPC, what should be delivered, and how success should be measured across diverse surgical environments.

items.title: Paper-first knowledge engineering as a pedagogical framework for cognitive agency in AI-assisted learning
items.abstract: This study investigates how a structured “paper-first” approach can support cognitive engagement during artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted academic work in higher education. Growing reliance on generative AI has increased concerns about surface-level learning, trial-and-error prompting, and reduced student ownership of academic writing. Using a two-year design-based research approach involving nine iterative cycles, the study developed and refined a framework that required students to construct manual logic diagrams before engaging with AI tools and expert system environments. Participants included a six-member interdisciplinary design team and 150 communication for academic purposes students from the faculty of information and communications technology at a South African university. Data were collected through iterative observations and focus group interviews and analyzed using grounded theory and constant comparative analysis. Findings indicate that the framework supported more structured reasoning, reduced inefficient prompting behaviors, and improved students’ ability to identify weaknesses in their own arguments before digital interaction. Students also reported increased confidence and greater ownership of their academic work. The study argues that structured pre-AI planning activities can strengthen critical thinking and academic literacy by positioning AI as a support tool rather than a substitute for cognitive effort. The findings contribute practical guidance for educators seeking to integrate AI into higher education while preserving student agency and deep learning.

items.title: Patterns of morphology in children’s print: estimates of polymorphemic vocabulary using an innovative, AI-informed database of British and American word families
items.abstract: Background Morphological complexity is a pervasive feature of the vocabulary children encounter in print, yet resources for investigating morphology remain limited. What morpheme patterns do children encounter in print? Which morphemes cover how many polymorphic words in reading experiences? In this study we introduce the British and American Word Families (BAWF) project, an innovative open database of ∼378,000 words, and use it to address questions such as these. Methods GPT-4.1 was fine-tuned using ∼6000 morphologically-coded words from an existing human-generated database (Morpholex). The fine-tuned LLM coded word-parts in all Wiktionary words attested in large British and American corpora. Performance was evaluated via agreement with existing databases. Classical roots were attributed to a subset of words by mapping a list of roots from Wikipedia to all related entries in Wiktionary. The resulting BAWF database is then used to estimate morpheme patterns across databases of children’s texts and further developed as an online application. Results LLM word part predictions are good and fall within the range of agreement typical of existing databases. Nonetheless, output contains some error/noise. In children’s print, polymorphemic words increase across picturebooks to juvenile fiction and school-reading programs. Greek-Latin root words occur early and commonly. Estimates include that ∼100 prefixes/suffixes may account for nearly all derivations. The BAWF itself is released open-source https://cgg-projects.github.io/BAWF_V1/ , with many lexical, morphological, and psycholinguistic variables, including but not limited to frequency, family size, and morpheme-counts. Discussion The contribution suggests that instruction that prioritizes high-yield morphemes could give children access to large word families. These morphemes are present and common early in print. The BAWF (V1) helps see which may be useful to teach. Users can generate custom wordlists, targeting particular features and families, and access linked dictionary/etymological information. The platform includes AI-assisted searches, explanations, parsing review/corrections, and instructional support. The BAWF project will develop over time, incorporating additional variables (e.g., morphological transparency), improving accuracy and the user interface.

items.title: PEDAGOGICAL CONDITIONS OF INTEGRATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND GEOINFORMATION SYSTEMS IN GEOGRAPHY EDUCATION
items.abstract: The article analyzes the pedagogical conditions for using the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and geographic information systems (GIS) in geography education from a theoretical and methodological perspective. The didactic possibilities of digital technologies in the processes of searching, sorting, spatial analysis, mapping and interpretation of geographical data are highlighted. The main pedagogical conditions are based on the combination of AI and GIS tools with educational goals, the development of students' geographical and digital competencies, the improvement of teacher methodological training and the improvement of educational resources. A methodological approach is also proposed to organize integrated education.

items.title: Pengaruh Artificial Intelligence dan Digital HRM terhadap Efektivitas Manajemen Sumber Daya Manusia: Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Transformasi digital mendorong organisasi mengintegrasikan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan Digital Human Resource Management (Digital HRM) dalam proses pengelolaan sumber daya manusia. AI dapat membantu analisis data, penyaringan kandidat, pembelajaran, serta evaluasi kinerja, sedangkan Digital HRM mendukung digitalisasi administrasi dan layanan SDM melalui sistem informasi yang terintegrasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkaji bagaimana AI dan Digital HRM berkontribusi terhadap efektivitas manajemen sumber daya manusia, sekaligus mengidentifikasi tantangan penerapannya. Artikel disusun melalui tinjauan literatur sistematis dengan fokus pada publikasi ilmiah tahun 2021–2025. Sumber ditelusuri melalui publikasi jurnal yang dapat diidentifikasi melalui DOI dan laman penerbit, dengan kata kunci terkait AI in HRM, digital HRM, e-HRM, HR technology, dan HRM effectiveness. Pemetaan awal literatur menunjukkan empat tema utama: efisiensi proses dan dukungan keputusan; penerimaan dan kesiapan organisasi; pengalaman serta peran profesional SDM; dan tata kelola yang bertanggung jawab. Literatur menunjukkan potensi peningkatan kecepatan proses, konsistensi layanan, dan dukungan keputusan, tetapi manfaat tersebut tidak terjadi secara otomatis. Kualitas data, kompetensi pengguna, transparansi algoritma, privasi, bias, serta kesesuaian teknologi dengan kebutuhan organisasi menjadi faktor penting. Kajian ini menyimpulkan bahwa AI dan Digital HRM sebaiknya diposisikan sebagai sarana pendukung strategi SDM, bukan pengganti pertimbangan manusia.

items.title: PERAN MEDIA SOSIAL INSTAGRAM BPBD DKI JAKARTA DALAM PENYAMPAIAN INFORMASI PERINGATAN DINI BENCANA KEPADA MASYARAKAT
items.abstract: Disaster early warning requires communication channels that can deliver accurate, timely, and actionable information to the public. This study examines the role of the official Instagram account of the DKI Jakarta Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD), @bpbddkijakarta, in disseminating disaster early warning information. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed. Data were collected through non-participant observation of disaster-related Instagram content, in-depth interviews, documentation, and literature review. Informants were selected purposively and consisted of the Head of the Disaster Data and Information Processing Unit, an expert who manages the BPBD DKI Jakarta Instagram account, and two community members who actively follow the account. The findings show that Instagram functions as a digital disaster communication channel through Feed, Stories, and Reels, supported by infographics, maps, photographs, and short videos. Early warning messages contain information on hazards, affected areas, warning periods, current conditions, public advisories, and recommended actions. Before publication, information is collected, processed, verified, and adapted into concise visual content according to urgency. For community informants, the account helps them monitor disaster conditions, adjust activities, and increase situational awareness. However, Instagram cannot reach all population groups because access depends on internet connectivity, social media use, and digital literacy. Therefore, Instagram is most appropriately positioned as part of a multi-channel disaster communication strategy rather than as a single early warning medium.

items.title: Perceived artificial intelligence dependence and anxiety symptoms among university students: a three-wave study of experiential avoidance and digital literacy
items.abstract: University students increasingly use artificial intelligence tools for learning, decision-making, and academic work, making perceived AI dependence a relevant issue for public mental health and digital public health rather than only for educational technology. This three-wave time-lagged survey examined whether experiential avoidance functioned as a putative explanatory process linking perceived AI dependence with later anxiety symptoms and whether digital literacy moderated the tested pathways. Online survey data were collected from 1,451 university students with AI-use experience; perceived AI dependence, digital literacy, and baseline demographic variables were measured in January 2026, experiential avoidance was measured in March 2026, and anxiety symptoms were measured in June 2026. PLS-SEM results showed that experiential avoidance was strongly and positively associated with later anxiety symptoms (beta = 0.677, p < 0.001), whereas the direct association between perceived AI dependence and anxiety symptoms was not significant (beta = -0.030, p = 0.147); perceived AI dependence was negatively associated with experiential avoidance (beta = -0.114, p < 0.001), producing a statistically significant but theoretically unexpected negative time-ordered indirect association (beta = -0.077, p < 0.001), and digital literacy did not significantly moderate the tested pathways. The findings suggest that anxiety symptoms in AI-mediated learning contexts are closely linked to avoidance-related psychological processes, while the meaning of perceived AI dependence is context-dependent and should not be equated automatically with harmful use or clinical addiction; campus mental-health promotion should therefore integrate responsible AI education with support for psychological flexibility, uncertainty tolerance, and autonomous learning.

items.title: Perceptions, practices and governance of generative AI in university social science teaching in Ecuador
items.abstract: The advent of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming academic production and confronting the social sciences with the challenge of preserving critical thinking in the face of mechanically generated content. This research examines the perceptions and practices of social science lecturers and students at Ecuadorian universities regarding the use of AI, together with their motivations, constraints and the institutional policies currently in force. A mixed-methods design was adopted, combining qualitative and quantitative approaches. The instruments comprised semi-structured interviews with lecturers and students at national and Ibero-American universities; a non-probabilistic survey of 200 students; and a content analysis of seven sets of regulations from universities in Ecuador, all aligned with the framework of competencies identified by UNESCO-IESALC. The results show a moderate-to-high level of AI use (mean = 3.68), explained by perceived usefulness and extrinsic motivation rather than ease of use, and a gap between the demand for regulation (4.00) and perceived regulatory clarity (3.21); only one of the seven universities has a policy formally designated as such, and ethics predominates over professional and disciplinary development. The study concludes that the governance of AI in Ecuadorian higher education requires an evaluative redesign and discipline-differentiated competencies.

items.title: Personalized Migraine Therapy Using Innovative Transdermal Drug Delivery System
items.abstract: Migraine is a prevalent and disabling neurological disorder characterized by recurrent headache attacks and associated symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, photophobia, and phonophobia. Conventional oral therapies may be limited by variable drug absorption, gastrointestinal disturbances, first-pass metabolism, delayed onset of action, and poor adherence, highlighting the need for individualized therapeutic approaches. Personalized migraine therapy integrates patient-specific factors, including genetic variability, hormonal status, comorbidities, migraine frequency, and treatment response, to optimize clinical outcomes. Transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) offer a promising platform for personalized migraine management by bypassing gastrointestinal and hepatic first-pass effects and enabling controlled and sustained drug release. Conventional patches, microneedles, iontophoresis, sonophoresis, electroporation, nanocarrier-based systems, and stimuli-responsive smart patches can enhance drug permeation and provide flexible dosing strategies. Biomarker-guided treatment, pharmacogenomics, and digital monitoring may further facilitate patient stratification and individualized patch selection. Emerging technologies integrating artificial intelligence, wearable sensors, nanomedicine, and closed-loop drug delivery could enable real-time adaptation of therapy according to patient needs. This review discusses the pathophysiological and molecular basis of migraine, principles of personalized medicine, innovative TDDS technologies, current clinical developments, challenges, and future perspectives, emphasizing their potential to improve therapeutic efficacy, safety, adherence, and patient-centered migraine care.

items.title: PFedQFT: Personalized Federated Quantum-Inspired Fine-Tuning for Medical Large Language Models
items.abstract: Medical data remain fragmented across institutional silos because of privacy, governance, and ownership constraints. Federated learning enables medical institutions to adapt large language models (LLMs) collaboratively without transferring raw records. However, independently parameterized low-rank adapters incur repeated parameter and communication costs across Transformer projections, while uniform aggregation may limit adaptation to heterogeneous institutional data. We propose PFedQFT, a quantum-inspired framework for personalized federated fine-tuning with a compact shared adapter. Specifically, PFedQFT constructs reusable orthonormal adaptation bases from compact skew-symmetric generators using a truncated matrix-exponential approximation followed by QR orthonormalization. Compatible projections reuse these bases, while a globally shared full core preserves the flexibility of each projection. Each client further maintains a lightweight private residual operator, whose directions are learned globally and whose coefficients remain local. Experiments on seven public medical tasks and multiple LLM backbones show substantial reductions in trainable parameters and per-round adapter upload volume, with competitive predictive performance on most tasks.

items.title: PhyPro-FM: A Physics and Prompt-Guided Graph Foundation Model for Contingency Analysis
items.abstract: The continuous evolution of next-generation power systems, characterized by the high penetration of renewable energy resources and dynamic topology variations, poses formidable challenges to traditional N-1/N-2 contingency analysis in terms of computational efficiency and scalability. While deep learning-based methods offer accelerated inference, existing studies predominantly treat contingency analysis as a pure regression problem, often overlooking the physical essence of grid operation and engineering requirements of real-world scenarios. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a physics and prompt-guided graph foundation model (PhyPro-FM) for generalizable and engineering-viable contingency analysis. The proposed architecture integrates graph neural networks with a learnable global query mechanism and, notably, introduces a prompt-guided learning paradigm. By leveraging historical snapshots as few-shot prompts, the model dynamically captures correlations between target and historical operating conditions, significantly enhancing generalization capabilities under unseen topologies. Furthermore, we design a physics-informed training mechanism that prioritizes branch power flow errors over nodal voltage errors, aligning the optimization objective with critical grid security constraints. To ensure engineering applicability, a physics-informed inference mechanism is also developed, incorporating a residual-based correction module and a specialized post-processing strategy for singular branches to circumvent numerical instability. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that PhyPro-FM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy and generalization, validating its superior physical consistency and robustness for practical engineering applications.

items.title: Physical AI: Concepts, Techniques, and Challenges
items.abstract: In recent years, physical artificial intelligence (physical AI) has experienced rapid development, capturing significant attention in academia and industry. However, the field has yet to reach consensus on its definition, technical landscape, and core challenges. To address this gap, this monograph seeks to define physical AI, present its technical landscape, and examine each key technical subfield in depth. In doing so, it establishes a unified framework for Physical AI: artificial systems that perceive, model, and act upon the physical world through continuous feedback under real-world constraints. Further, this monograph distinguishes physical AI from conventional digital AI, embodied AI, cyber-physical systems, and digital twins. It develops the foundations of physical AI across physics, control, cognition, learning, and reasoning. It reviews key methodologies, including multimodal perception, physical data and simulation, world models, embodied foundation models, motor-control systems, multi-agent coordination, and hardware-software co-design. Furthermore, it examines applications spanning robotics, manufacturing, infrastructure, scientific experimentation, and autonomous services. Particular attention is given to sim-to-real transfer, reliability, real-time execution, evaluation, safety, governance, and long-term deployment. By connecting perception, prediction, decision-making, action, and adaptation in a closed loop, this monograph identifies the technical challenges and research directions required to advance from narrow automation toward more generalizable physical AI and, ultimately, physical artificial general intelligence (Physical AGI).

items.title: Pilot Fatigue and Flight Safety Performance in Commercial Airlines
items.abstract: Pilot fatigue is one of the most pervasive and consequential human factors hazards in commercial aviation worldwide. This study examines the relationship between pilot fatigue and flight safety performance in the context of Nigerian commercial aviation, where domestic short-haul operations, irregular scheduling, and evolving regulatory frameworks create a complex operational environment. Drawing on a quantitative survey of 142 active commercial pilots operating out of Lagos, Abuja, and Kano, combined with a secondary analysis of occurrence reports from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), this research investigates the prevalence, contributing factors, and safety consequences of pilot fatigue. Results indicate that 71.1% of respondents reported operationally significant fatigue on their most recent duty day, while 95.1% reported at least one such episode in the preceding three months, with inadequate rest periods, multiple short-haul flight legs per duty period, and irregular scheduling identified as the primary antecedents. Multiple regression analysis showed associations such that flight legs per duty day (β = 0.41, p < .001), early start frequency (β = 0.33, p < .001), and weekly duty hours (β = 0.29, p = .002) were the strongest operational predictors of fatigue severity (R² = .573 full model). Fatigue-associated occurrences were linked to lapses in situational awareness, procedural deviations, and communication errors in the cockpit. The study recommends accelerated adoption of Fatigue Risk Management Systems (FRMS), strengthened enforcement of Nigeria Civil Aviation Regulations (NCARs) flight and duty time limitations, and industry-wide fatigue reporting culture improvements. Findings contribute to the growing body of evidence on fatigue in sub-Saharan African aviation contexts and inform policy for regulators and airline operators.

items.title: Platformization of Professional Governance
items.abstract: This chapter examines the platformization of professional governance and its implications for expertise, authority, and self-regulation in technologically saturated societies. It argues that digital platforms and artificial intelligence (AI) are not merely tools augmenting professional practice, but active intermediaries that restructure knowledge production, labor processes, and governance arrangements. Through algorithmic management, data extraction, and rating systems, platforms introduce novel mechanisms of surveillance and control that blur the boundaries between managerial oversight and professional autonomy. The analysis highlights how AI simultaneously augments and displaces expertise, reshaping task design, skill requirements, and professional identities. Platformization alters traditional forms of social closure, educational credentialling, and state-based regulation, while fostering new forms of mediated self-governance, particularly in emerging platform-based professions. At the same time, corporate ownership of digital infrastructures and large language models raises critical questions about epistemic authority, accountability, and the governance of expert knowledge. This chapter concludes that professional governance is increasingly hybrid and contested, shaped by interactions between state regulation, market logics, and platform-based algorithmic systems, and that safeguarding professional integrity in this evolving landscape requires renewed empirical and theoretical attention to the governance of AI-driven expertise.

items.title: Platforms as architects of AI influence: rethinking moderation in the age of hybrid expression
items.abstract: The widespread availability of generative AI has reshaped how content is created, circulated, and governed across social media platforms. As users experiment with synthetic media—remixing, reposting, and negotiating hybrid communicative practices_platforms have emerged as central agents in the AI attention economy, forging lucrative partnerships and developing proprietary features that shape how AI content is legitimised. This article proposes that conventional human rights frameworks, particularly freedom of expression, are ill-equipped to govern increasingly hybrid media, where authorship and provenance are fluid, and emerging dilemmas hinge more on perceived value than rights violations. Within this context, spam policies operate as under-scrutinised instruments of discretionary control, enabling platforms to curate visibility and legitimacy through opaque mechanisms. Drawing on Reddit’s provenance-agnostic, participatory moderation model, the article proposes that collective negotiation by online communities—around what constitutes valuable or acceptable content—offers a more transparent, context-sensitive, and adaptive approach to moderation of hybrid human-AI expression.

items.title: Pocket AI Stylist — Technical Report
items.abstract: We report a measured deployment of a server-side rendered (SSR) e-commerce storefront on a serverless edge platform, and propose a grounded, LLM-based recommender for footwear. The Pocket Shoes is a curated online shoe store operating in Vietnam since 2020. Its Nuxt 4 storefront was moved from a single virtual machine to Cloudflare Workers. Over 24 hours of production traffic, median SSR CPU time was 66.95 ms per request (P99 155 ms), 6.7 times the 10 ms budget of the free tier, while memory stayed under 15 MB. We describe an edge HTML cache built on the platform Cache API that skips pages whose server-side data fetch failed, so transient backend errors are never served from cache. We then present the design of Pocket AI Stylist: shoe discovery from a photo, from a short lifestyle questionnaire, or from a conversation, where a multimodal large language model (LLM) extracts style attributes, a hybrid retriever restricts candidates to in-stock items in the shopper's size, and the LLM re-ranks and explains only those candidates. We define an offline and online evaluation protocol. The AI system is in development; this report contains no AI evaluation results. items.title: PORA: Learning When More Reasoning Pays Off for LLM Agents
items.abstract: LLM agents perform tasks over multiple steps and revise their actions based on feedback. As the total reasoning budget is often limited and must support future steps, the agent must choose between short and long reasoning before each action. Longer reasoning may improve the final task outcome by preventing later errors, but it also uses budget capacity that may be needed for future decisions. This creates two challenges: estimating the downstream value of long reasoning and deciding when that value is worth using the remaining budget. We propose Paired Outcome-guided Reasoning Allocation (PORA), which learns this decision by comparing short and long reasoning from the same interaction state. During training, \method{} completes the task twice from each selected state, once with a short reasoning allowance and once with a long allowance, and compares their final quality and total processing to estimate when longer reasoning is valuable. During inference, a controller weighs this estimate against learned prices on remaining-budget pressure and chooses either short or long reasoning without running both alternatives. We evaluate PORA across application, memory, code, retail, and mathematics tasks, achieving strong results across all settings. On BFCL memory, it exceeds the strongest existing method by 17.4--32.9 percentage points. Within the same agent, it matches or exceeds always using long reasoning on code and mathematics with 50.6% fewer actor tokens and 31.2% fewer model requests, respectively.

items.title: Practical Pathways for Optimizing Rural Communication Networks in Mountainous Areas Using Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Aiming at weak communication network coverage and low-efficiency manual network optimization (NRO) troubleshooting in mountainous rural areas, this paper proposes an artificial intelligence (AI) assisted NRO approach, constructing a human-machine collaborative workflow: "AI simulation pre-judgment, data preliminary screening, engineer on-site recheck, closed-loop iterative optimization." AI leverages massive data processing for coverage simulation, poor-quality user mining, tidal traffic analysis, and geological hazard identification to narrow manual inspection scope; engineers conduct targeted rectification and feed measured data back to correct model deviations. This study selects typical mountainous townships in Hanzhong as pilot, integrating multi-source data including measurement reports (MR), base-station engineering parameters, traffic key performance indicators (KPI), user complaint tickets, and digital elevation model (DEM). AI pre-screening output 42 points to be checked; after on-site recheck, 14 false alarms were removed and 28 real problems confirmed. Optimization effects were compared across network quality, user perception, O&M workload, and hazard early-warning dimensions. Implementation constraints including model bias, outdated equipment, talent shortage, funding insufficiency, and data barriers are analyzed, with countermeasures proposed from operation mechanism, hardware iteration, talent cultivation, resource coordination, and data governance dimensions, providing reference for large-scale AI application in rural communication NRO.

items.title: Precision Nutrition and Health Outcomes Across the Lifespan
items.abstract: Precision nutrition is an emerging paradigm that seeks to tailor dietary recommendations and interventions based on individual and population characteristics. Although advances in multi-omics, wearable sensors, and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) have accelerated discovery, translation into practice remains limited by fragmented evidence across life stages and insufficient integration of knowledge regarding systems biology and other influences on health. Nutritional needs, vulnerabilities, intervention opportunities, and response heterogeneity evolve dynamically from preconception and pregnancy through infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older age. These life stage-specific processes intersect with (epi)genetic, metabolic and microbiome factors, as well as social, psychological, behavioral, and environmental/geographic influences, contributing to heterogeneity in health outcomes. Addressing this complexity requires not only multimodal predictive models but also frameworks that integrate data standards and harmonization, systems biology, implementation science, and community engagement. To provide a structured approach to this complexity, we developed a seven-pillar Precision Nutrition Framework encompassing prevention for all, data sources, quantitative sciences, qualitative sciences, intervention implementation, communities, and education and workforce training. Using this framework and a lifespan perspective, we examine opportunities for promoting cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematologic, and circadian/sleep health, synthesize evidence on key nutrients, dietary patterns, and emerging biomarkers, and adapt and expand the “precision nutrition plate” for implementation research in clinical and community settings. We highlight critical research gaps, including the need for phenotype-guided trials, standardized data integration, and scalable implementation strategies. By integrating biological, behavioral, and broader environmental dimensions across the life course, precision nutrition can advance more effective, accessible, and sustainable approaches for disease prevention and health promotion.

items.title: Predicting Passing-Play Outcomes in American Football: A Comparative Study of Traditional Machine Learning Algorithms and Fine-Tuned Large Language Models
items.abstract: This study examines American football passing play strategies based on an analysis of 100 NFL games, addressing the notable lack of research on offensive passing strategies. The yardage prediction task is formulated as a regression task, and the touchdown prediction task is formulated as a classification task. A regression analysis was conducted using four traditional machine learning models, including Support Vector Machines (SVMs), K-Nearest Neighbors, XGBoost, and LightGBM, and a LoRA-fine-tuned Llama 3 (8B) model. The SVM model showed optimal performance with a Mean Absolute Error of 6.996 yards, marginally outperforming the Llama 3 model (7.059 yards). In contrast, the fine-tuned Llama 3 significantly outperformed all traditional algorithms for the classification task, with a Macro F1 of 0.712 compared to the highest Macro F1 of 0.614 for traditional algorithms. Therefore, I advocate large language models (LLMs) for classification tasks and traditional machine learning algorithms for regression tasks. Sports analytics models can be selected based on the findings of these studies.

items.title: Predictive basket steering and shopper choice sovereignty in AI-enabled retailing: A self-determination theory perspective
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence becomes embedded in online retailing, personalization systems increasingly shape consumers’ shopping baskets rather than merely recommend products. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory, this study examines how predictive basket steering is associated with shopper choice sovereignty and retailer reliance comfort among Chinese online grocery shoppers. Predictive steering is conceptualized through three mechanisms: option pruning convenience, preference reflection accuracy, and commercial intent transparency. Survey data from 483 shoppers were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, with post-stratification calibration to national demographic benchmarks. The results indicate that predictive steering is positively associated with all three mechanisms, and each mechanism is positively associated with shopper choice sovereignty. Preference reflection accuracy and transparency are also directly associated with retailer reliance comfort, whereas option pruning convenience has no direct association with reliance comfort. Shopper choice sovereignty, in turn, is strongly associated with retailer reliance comfort. The study contributes to AI-enabled retailing research by highlighting that convenience alone is insufficient for comfortable reliance; rather, perceived decision authorship (sovereignty) is the central mechanism. It suggests that effective basket steering should combine convenience and personalized relevance with transparent, revisable, and consumer-controlled choice architecture.

items.title: Predictive modeling and optimization of eco-friendly cementitious grouts containing waste marble dust for semi-flexible pavements
items.abstract: Semi-flexible pavements integrate the advantages of flexible and rigid systems through a porous asphalt layer filled with cement-based grout; however, their high cement consumption raises environmental concerns. This study aims to optimize eco-friendly cementitious grouts incorporating waste marble dust (WMD) using machine learning techniques based on 72 experimental mixtures. The dataset included water–cement ratios (0.35–0.50), WMD content (0–25%), grout flow, and compressive strengths at 7 (CS_7d) and 28 days (CS_28d). Five machine learning models, including artificial neural networks (ANN), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and k-nearest neighbor (KNN) were developed and evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE), coefficient of determination (R 2 ), and adjusted R 2 . Among these, the decision tree model demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy with R² = 0.994 and MAE = 0.266 MPa. Explainable artificial intelligence methods, including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and partial dependence plots (PDPs), identified 7-day compressive strength as the most influential parameter, as it provides an experimentally measured representation of the early-age strength development of the grout. Results indicate that increasing water–cement ratio and marble dust content reduces CS_28d. Model-based optimization allowed up to 32% cement replacement at a 0.4 water–cement ratio with 0.5% superplasticizer, while higher ratios reduced replacement efficiency. The findings demonstrate the potential of WMD as a partial cement replacement in semi-flexible pavement grout, supporting waste valorization and reducing cement demand while providing a data-driven approach for sustainable mixture design.

items.abstract: Background: Sugarcane processing requires intensive physical labor, exposing workers to manual material handling, repetitive trunk movements, and prolonged awkward postures.While India's sugar sector is vast, systematic occupational health surveillance within processing mills remains limited.This study evaluates the 12-month prevalence of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) and quantifies physical risk profiles among factory workers in Maharashtra.Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted from August 2025 to February 2026 among 416 workers across two manufacturing facilities in the Sangli district.The Standardised Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ) tracked regional symptom distribution.Postural and task-specific ergonomic risks were measured using the Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) and the Quick Exposure Checklist (QEC).Labourers were categorised into four operational task groups.Bivariate associations were assessed using Pearson Chi-square tests, and independent predictors of regional symptoms were determined via multivariable logistic regression.Results: The highest 12-month symptom prevalence rates were observed in the lower back (69.95%),shoulder (69.23%), and upper back (67.07%).No participants fell within the negligible or low REBA risk tiers; 83.1% were classified as high or very high risk.Postural risk scores did not vary significantly across departments (mean REBA range: 9.5-9.8;Kruskal-Wallis H = 1.484, p = 0.686).Overweight workers (BMI ≥ 25 kg/m²) had significantly higher odds of hip/thigh symptoms (OR = 1.85; 95% CI: 1.25-2.73;p = 0.002).High or very high QEC exposure profiles correlated significantly with shoulder (OR = 2.08, p = 0.029) and ankle/foot symptoms (OR = 2.18, p = 0.021).In multivariable models, continuous BMI (aOR = 1.094; 95% CI: 1.032-1.159;p = 0.003) and younger age (aOR = 0.970; 95% CI: 0.950-0.990;p = 0.004) independently predicted hip/thigh symptoms.Conclusion: Sugarcane processing workers face severe, uniform ergonomic hazards that transcend specific job assignments.The high symptom burden emphasises the need for comprehensive, facility-wide ergonomic adjustments and targeted preventive physical therapy programs.

items.title: Productive State-Space Exploration for Multi-turn RL in LLM Agents
items.abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) for Large Language Model (LLM) agents in multi-turn, long-horizon environments remains challenging due to inefficient action selection and repetitive behavioral patterns. In particular, agents often become trapped in high-confidence yet unproductive behaviors, repeatedly executing invalid actions or entering action loops that hinder task completion. We observe that these frequently violate environment preconditions, revealing a mismatch between the agent's representation of the internal state and the dynamics of the underlying environment. In addition, repetitive high-confidence actions lead to cyclical behaviors that provide little to no progress towards the goal. We argue that addressing these challenges requires more productive task-aligned exploration to improve the agent's understanding of environment dynamics. Motivated by intrinsic curiosity-driven exploration, we propose a conditional state-space exploration framework that balances task completion with intrinsic information-seeking behavior. Specifically, we introduce an intrinsic reward that penalizes actions whose observation duplicates prior state memory. This provides the benefit of reducing redundant behaviors and encouraging state-space coverage without relying on a general information-theoretic measure. Strong experimental results demonstrate that our approach substantially improves policy learning in multi-turn environments, mitigating invalid actions and repetitive loops.

items.title: Profile-DP: Differential Privacy for User-Controlled Profile Release in Personalized LLM Inference
items.abstract: Personalized large language models (LLMs) increasingly rely on profile-conditioned inference, pairing public requests with rich, user-specific facts. This paradigm exposes the user profile itself, together with the user's explicit sharing preferences. We introduce Profile-DP, a policy-aware local differential privacy framework designed specifically for user-profile release in personalized LLM inference. Profile-DP provably bounds the release of user-withheld facts while treating public instructions, profile schemas, and authorized facts as public side information. By generating a privatized profile that composes with the public instruction prior to answer generation, our framework decouples formal privacy guarantees from downstream model behavior. We develop two finite-domain mechanisms satisfying Profile-DP: DP-SLOT independently perturbs protected attributes, while DP-BLOCK uses public semantic decisions to coordinate their release and jointly sample related attributes. A positive, public compatibility prior connects these attributes while preserving a profile-level privacy bound. On PEEP, DP-BLOCK leads the utility composite among DP methods at all 13 structured budgets and is closest to the ideal privacy--utility point in 18 of 26 format--budget settings under our composite weighting. Direct measurements reveal complementary strengths: DP-BLOCK discloses less, while DP-SLOT retains more authorized facts. These results make policy-aware profile release a practical basis for studying privacy and personalization.

items.title: ProMemAgent: Long-Horizon Proactive Assistance with Context-Aware Prospective Memory from Sensory Perceptions
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are moving beyond reactive responses toward proactive assistance that anticipates user needs without explicit requests. However, existing proactive agents primarily address immediate needs, while many everyday situations involve delayed intentions that can only be acted on hours or days later. Humans handle such intentions through prospective memory, the ability to remember to act on an intention when the right moment arises. In this paper, we introduce ProMemAgent, the first proactive agent to incorporate prospective memory over everyday sensory contexts for long-horizon proactive assistance. ProMemAgent organizes past sensory perceptions (e.g., egocentric video and audio) into context-aware memory, generating prospective cues and linking earlier events with subsequent developments for future retrieval. Given the current context, it retrieves relevant past events and performs memory-augmented proactive reasoning to determine whether assistance is needed. We further introduce CPMBench, the first benchmark for evaluating long-horizon proactive assistance over sensory contexts, comprising 1,000 instances across eight everyday categories. Extensive experiments show that ProMemAgent achieves the best memory retrieval performance and consistently outperforms all baselines on long-horizon proactive assistance.

items.title: Promptile: Recovering and Reusing Prompting Strategies from LLM Interaction Histories
items.abstract: As people use large language models (LLMs) over time, they develop their own ways of prompting to achieve desired results. These useful experiences often remain scattered and unorganized across conversations. Yet existing personalization approaches primarily capture user preferences or explicitly defined workflows. Through a formative study, we found that users develop prompting strategies that range from implicit instructions to explicit templates from these experiences. We further find that interaction behaviors provide evidence for these strategies, which can be decomposed and recombined for reuse across tasks. Building on these findings, we present Promptile, a framework that identifies and validates users' prompting strategies from interaction histories. Promptile organizes these strategies into reusable components that can be retrieved, combined, and adapted to users' current tasks. Our evaluation shows that Promptile accurately recovers and reuses these strategies, better aligning model outputs with users' expectations while reducing repetitive prompting effort.

items.title: Prompts for the two AI-peer stances: supplementary material for "Consensus or Debate? Interactional Patterns of Idea Development with AI Peers in Collaborative Discussion"
items.abstract: Supplementary material for the paper "Consensus or Debate? Interactional Patterns of Idea Development with AI Peers in Collaborative Discussion" (under review).The document reproduces, verbatim, the prompts that drove the AI peer in a Wizard-of-Oz study of small-group discussions. A large language model (Gemini 2.5 Flash) periodically assessed the conversation with an assessment prompt and, when an intervention seemed warranted, drafted one with a generation prompt; a human Wizard then sent, edited or dismissed it. Two stances were compared: ConsensusBot, which synthesised ideas and moved the group toward agreement, and DebateBot, a devil's advocate that probed premature agreement and unchallenged claims. items.title: Proof-of-Machine-Learning-Inference: Mining Knowledge, Not Hashes
items.abstract: Bitcoin-style Proof-of-Work (PoW) secures permissionless blockchains but spends substantial computation on hash puzzles which have no utility other than extending the chain. At the same time, we have seen that the rise of generative AI has created significant demand for computational resources that are unfortunately available only to a few players. We propose a solution that solves both problems at the same time. In particular, we present Proof-of-ML-Inference (PoML), a consensus protocol in which miners perform user-requested machine-learning inference as part of their consensus algorithm. We identify exactly what computational assumptions are needed for ML inference to safely replace hash work, formalize those assumptions, and give evidence that LLMs and diffusion models satisfy them. We then formally analyse the security of our protocol by reducing the security of our protocol to the security of the Bitcoin Backbone model. Finally, we empirically evaluate block-time stability, showing that, in a simulated environment, PoML maintains a block production rate close to its calibrated block-time target.

items.abstract: This study describes the cognitive, affective, and social adaptation of seventh-grade students without a Madrasah Ibtidaiyah (MI) background as they begin learning Arabic at Madrasah Tsanawiyah (MTs), and identifies the factors that support or hinder that adaptation. A qualitative case study design was used, informed by Piaget's concept of adaptation (assimilation, accommodation, and equilibration). Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with three Arabic teachers and six purposively selected non-MI students, supported by classroom observation and document analysis, and were analysed with the Miles and Huberman interactive model and validated through source and method triangulation. The findings show that non-MI students initially experienced cognitive disorientation, particularly in translating vocabulary (mufradat) and grasping morphological concepts such as gender (mudzakkar-muannats) and plural forms. Affective responses were mixed, ranging from anxiety and shyness to neutral first reactions. Socially, peer support was the most relied-upon adaptation resource, ahead of direct teacher help, and no bullying of non-MI students was reported. Adaptation proceeded through an orientation stage, an adjustment stage in which students and teachers developed coping strategies, and a partial stabilisation stage, although reading fluency and vocabulary translation remained the slowest skills to stabilise. Supporting factors included peer assistance, teachers' personal guidance, Arabic vocabulary displayed around the school, and speech (muhadarah) activities; inhibiting factors included low intrinsic motivation, limited prior exposure, uneven family support, and limited projector access. The study proposes untested practical recommendations, including a structured matriculation period.

items.title: Protease Signatures in Health and Disease: Toward Smart Diagnostic Platforms
items.abstract: Abstract Proteases, a vast and functionally diverse class of enzymes, are fundamental regulators of many important biological processes. Their activity is tightly controlled in cells; aberrant protease activity is associated with numerous pathologies including cancer, infectious diseases, neurodegeneration, and metabolic disorders. Protease dysregulation is not necessarily a mere consequence of disease but often a critical driver of pathogenesis, making protease activity a powerful functional biomarker. Importantly, protease activity offers a dynamic readout of biological function, integrating upstream regulatory signals with local environmental conditions. This Perspective explores the field of protease-based diagnostics, charting its evolution from fundamental research to emerging clinical applications. We first establish the rationale for using proteases as functional biomarkers across a spectrum of diseases, with particular focus on oncology, infectious diseases, neurodegeneration, and diabetes mellitus. Current and emerging technologies for detecting protease activity are then critically evaluated, from traditional substrate-based assays to sophisticated mass spectrometry platforms and innovative biosensing strategies involving smart probes, nanotechnology, and synthetic biology; we distinguish approaches that are clinically established from those validated in human samples, demonstrated preclinically, or still at the proof-of-concept stage. We then discuss the translational potential and inherent challenges of the approaches. Finally, we examine how multiplexed, activity-based profiling could generate dynamic “protease signatures” that, when combined with appropriate statistical and artificial intelligence methods, may support early disease detection, longitudinal monitoring, patient stratification, and personalized therapeutic strategies. Despite significant challenges related to biological complexity, analytical specificity, and clinical translation, protease diagnostics have the potential to provide disease information that complements established biomarkers and imaging modalities and may contribute to precision medicine.

items.title: PROVISO: Provenance-Informed Action Selection for Secure LLM Agents
items.abstract: LLM agents act on the external world through tools and third-party skills, so a single executed action can cause irreversible harm. Existing defenses judge a proposed action without tracking whether its content comes from the user or from external sources such as tool outputs, and they judge it in isolation rather than against an available alternative, which forces a trade-off between security and utility. We present PROVISO, a controller that decides which action to commit after the agent proposes an action and before it is executed. PROVISO encodes trusted observations, external observations, the proposed action, and an alternative into provenance-typed memory, relates them through role-specific queries, and commits the action with the highest calibrated value learned from outcomes. On four agent security tasks spanning the agent lifecycle, no baseline exceeds PROVISO in both security and utility. PROVISO improves F1 over the strongest baseline by 13.84 points on SkillsBench and by 7.07 points on ToolSafe, and it reaches 88-99 F1 on three additional skill detection benchmarks.

items.title: Pseudoparousia Theory: Why People Confide in Artificial Intelligence, and Why Confiding Is Not Enough
items.abstract: People increasingly confide their most dangerous thoughts to artificial intelligence (AI). Studies report that users disclose suicidal ideation more readily to conversational agents than to standard questionnaires or to other people, and platform data suggest that more than a million people each week discuss suicide with a single general-purpose chatbot. Yet this unprecedented volume of disclosure has not translated into proportionate protection, and some of the most serious harms associated with AI in mental health have occurred precisely within relationships of intense disclosure. This article proposes Pseudoparousia Theory (from the Greek pseudo-, false, and parousia, presence) to explain this paradox. The theory holds that disclosure seeks not only a listener but a presence: an other who is affected by what is disclosed, able to act on it, and continuous and accountable over time. Conversational AI produces the experience of presence – attention, responsiveness, apparent empathy, constant availability – without its substance. This counterfeit presence, or pseudoparousia, lowers the cost of disclosure for exactly the reasons that it removes disclosure’s protective consequences. The theory defines presence through three components (affectedness, agency, and continuity), distinguishes four configurations of witnessing (embodied presence, echo, deflection, and absence), formulates six propositions, and derives testable hypotheses, a measurement program, and implications for design, clinical practice, and regulation. Its central claim is that the decisive question for AI in mental health is not how accurately a system can detect distress, but whether presence can be transferred from the machine to a person in time.

items.title: Psychological and Behavioral Modeling: A Structured Review of Methods, Datasets, Applications, and Open Challenges
items.abstract: Psychological and behavioral modeling turns cognition, emotion, and motivation into computable quantities that can be related to observable behavior. The field has moved from theory-driven rules to statistical machine learning, deep learning, large language models (LLMs), and foundation models of cognition, but methods are fragmented, results are seldom comparable, and the link between opaque predictors and psychological theory is unsettled. This structured narrative review, reported with a PRISMA-style selection flow and an explicit evidence-tier coding, frames the field as a multilevel system. It organizes research into five modeling classes (psychological states, behavioral capabilities, individual–environment interaction, individual dynamics, and group psychology), defined by unit of analysis, target, and direction of inference, and it positions system dynamics, in the stock–flow–feedback sense, as one model family within that scheme rather than as a synonym for dynamical-systems modeling. We score the computational readiness of the theories that supply model ontologies on two rubric-based axes, formal specification and measurement maturity, and compare model families by assumptions, data needs, interpretability, and failure modes. Four claims are defended, each with stated boundary conditions and counterexamples: theory readiness, not algorithmic capability, determines where theory-informed learning is feasible; the dominant use of models shifts from individual-level estimation to collective-level simulation without a parallel shift in validation; multilevel data, not model capacity, constrain cross-scale modeling; and readiness claims must be indexed to a graded evidence base. We catalogue datasets, including small-group, dyadic, and longitudinal-network resources, review applications in mental health, education, decision support, and emergency management with their evidentiary status made explicit, treat military use as an ethically bounded case, and turn five recurrent bottlenecks into research-practice recommendations paired, where possible, with testable predictions.
